article.headline: OVR's Crowdsourced 3D Map Is Real, Its Claims Less So
article.lede: A small Italian startup called Over the Reality is assembling a georegistered, machine-readable database of the physical world, built not from satellite fleets or survey vehicles but from consumer cameras carried by incentivized volunteers. The company claims 220,000 scanned locations and a petabyte of spatial data — a genuine achievement in crowdsourced mapping, though its assertion of the world's first city-scale 3D map does not survive comparison with what Niantic, Google, or Apple have already built. The more interesting question is whether decentralized incentives can produce spatial data that matters for the next generation of AI systems.
article.body:
Over the Reality (OVR), a startup founded in Udine, Italy around 2019, is assembling what it describes as a machine-readable replica of the physical world. The method is notable for its low overhead: volunteer mappers walk through streets and buildings with a consumer 360-degree camera — here the Insta360 X5, a $550 spherical device capable of 72-megapixel, 8K spherical video — while OVR's software processes the footage into georegistered *Gaussian Splats*, photorealistic 3D scene representations that serve as reference imagery for AI systems. The company reports 220,000 mapped locations, 97 million images, and roughly one petabyte of spatial data; a live homepage counter had already ticked past 236,000 locations and 1,061 terabytes by May 2026. These figures are self-reported and unaudited, and the methodology for calculating terabyte totals is not disclosed.

The engine driving that growth is **Map2Earn**, a reward mechanism in which participating mappers receive OVR's native cryptocurrency token, worth roughly $0.90 to $3 per accepted submission. This places OVR in the *DePIN* category — Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Networks — in which blockchain incentives crowdsource the construction of real-world data infrastructure. The model is producing measurable results: the location count more than doubled between January 2025 and May 2026. The structural tension is that the underlying $OVR token trades at roughly four cents — down 99 percent from its 2021 peak of about four dollars — which materially weakens the economic case for new mappers at the very moment the company is making its largest scale claims.

The company's assertion of the "first global city-scale 3D map" overstates the case by a considerable margin. **Niantic Spatial** — spun out of the gaming company Niantic in May 2025, after Scopely acquired Niantic's games division for $3.5 billion — has catalogued 10 million georegistered locations comprising 30 billion positioned images, assembled over more than a decade by players of *Pokémon GO* and *Ingress*. Alphabet (GOOGL), through Google Maps, offers photorealistic 3D tiles covering more than 2,500 cities across 50 countries via aerial *photogrammetry* and a global StreetView fleet. Apple (AAPL) operates its own survey-vehicle and drone-based 3D coverage. CoStar Group (CSGP) completed its acquisition of Matterport in early 2025 for approximately $1.6 billion, adding a library of 14 million digitized indoor spaces — a different use case but overlapping ambition. OVR's defensible claim is narrower: the largest community-contributed 3D dataset built on a decentralized, open-incentive model.

What OVR is actually selling to developers is a *Visual Positioning System* (VPS) — a service that matches a query image submitted by a phone or robot camera against the company's georegistered reference library to return a position and orientation accurate to centimeters, far exceeding the three-to-five-metre accuracy typical of GPS. The technology is real and the market is growing. Hexagon (HEXA-B.ST), which owns the VPS specialist Immersal, launched city-scale VPS commercially in Helsinki, Tokyo, Seoul, and San Francisco in 2023, selling through mobile network operators. Niantic Spatial signed its first commercial robotics deployment — with the delivery-robot operator Coco Robotics — in early 2026. OVR's differentiation is the density of its community-sourced location database for indoor and pedestrian environments that satellite or aerial mapping cannot easily reach.

OVR has also announced a *Large Geospatial Model* (LGM) — an AI trained on its multiview image dataset, intended to let machines infer 3D structure and position from two-dimensional inputs, with eventual applications in robotics navigation. The LGM is on the roadmap, not in production. Its framing reflects a deliberate strategic pivot away from the "augmented reality metaverse" language that attracted capital in 2021 toward *Physical AI*, the dominant investment narrative in spatial computing as of 2025. The reframe is shrewd. Whether a twenty-person team backed primarily by crypto-native funds — EV3 Ventures, Modular Capital, Lattice — can execute at the scale required to matter against a competitor with 40 times its location count remains an open question.

concepts.definition: A real-time 3D scene representation technique that encodes a captured environment as millions of small, semi-transparent ellipsoids (Gaussian 'splats') derived from photographs or video. Unlike polygon meshes, splats capture fine detail and lighting with photorealistic results and can be rendered interactively on consumer hardware, making them attractive for AR, spatial computing, and machine-vision reference databases.

Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Networks — a blockchain-based model in which cryptocurrency rewards incentivize individuals to contribute physical resources (sensors, bandwidth, mapped locations) to build shared infrastructure. Participants earn tokens for each verified contribution; the resulting network is collectively governed by token holders rather than a single operator. OVR uses this model to crowdsource 3D spatial data.

OVR's crowdsourcing reward mechanism: volunteers capture video of physical locations using approved cameras, submit the footage to OVR's reconstruction pipeline, and receive $OVR cryptocurrency tokens upon acceptance of the resulting 3D map. The payout per accepted location ranges from approximately $0.90 to $3, making the system economically sensitive to the token's market price.

A localization technology that estimates a device's precise position and orientation by matching a live camera image against a database of georegistered reference photographs. Unlike GPS, which achieves roughly 3–5 metre accuracy and fails indoors, VPS can reach centimetre-level accuracy and functions inside buildings, making it useful for AR content anchoring, indoor navigation, and robot localization in GPS-denied environments.

The technique of deriving precise 3D measurements and models from sets of overlapping photographs. In city-scale mapping, aerial photogrammetry uses thousands of images captured from aircraft or satellites to reconstruct building facades, rooftops, and terrain. Ground-level photogrammetry applies the same principles with cameras on vehicles, drones, or handheld devices to capture street-level or indoor geometry.

An AI model trained on large datasets of georegistered imagery and 3D reconstructions, analogous to large language models but for spatial understanding. The goal is to enable a machine to infer 3D structure, camera position, and scene identity from a single or small set of 2D images — a capability useful for robotic navigation and AR localization without requiring exhaustive pre-mapped reference data at every location.

A term popularized by NVIDIA and others from 2024 onward for AI systems that operate in and reason about the physical, three-dimensional world — robots, autonomous vehicles, embodied agents. It contrasts with AI that processes only text or images, and reflects an investment thesis that the next frontier of AI capability requires rich spatial and sensory understanding of real environments.

article.fact_check: OVR's claim to have built 'the first global, city-scale 3D map' is materially misleading on multiple dimensions. Niantic Spatial's database covers 10 million georegistered locations (vs. OVR's ~236,000 — roughly 42 times larger) and 30 billion positioned images (vs. OVR's ~100 million — roughly 300 times larger), assembled years before OVR's dataset reached its current scale. Google Maps has offered photorealistic 3D coverage of more than 2,500 cities for several years. 'City-scale' also mischaracterizes OVR's product: the database consists of discrete point-of-interest scans (a storefront, a building entrance) rather than a continuous urban mesh. The dataset statistics OVR publishes are live self-reported counters with no disclosed methodology for the terabyte calculation or independent audit.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi's 2026 Stock Moves — Motley Fool

ticker_aapl.name: Apple Inc.
ticker_aapl.blurb: Apple designs and markets consumer electronics (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch), software, and digital services. The iPhone remains the dominant revenue driver, but the Services segment — comprising the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, Apple Pay, and licensing — has grown into a high-margin business that Wall Street values separately. Apple commands one of the highest brand loyalty rates in consumer technology and operates a tightly integrated hardware-software ecosystem.
ticker_aapl.recent: Apple reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $400 billion. The company has faced headwinds from slowing iPhone upgrade cycles in mature markets and regulatory pressure on App Store commissions in both the US and EU. Apple Intelligence, its generative AI suite, launched in late 2024 but has not yet materially re-accelerated upgrade cycles. Paul Pelosi sold 45,000 shares of AAPL according to the January 2026 PTR disclosure — the largest single sale in the filing by share count.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi Stock Tracker

ticker_csgp.name: CoStar Group, Inc.
ticker_csgp.blurb: CoStar Group is a leading provider of commercial real estate information, analytics, and online marketplaces. Its platforms include CoStar, LoopNet, and Apartments.com, serving brokers, investors, and property managers. The company holds a dominant market position in property data and listing services.
ticker_csgp.recent: In the past 30 days, CoStar Group reported Q4 2024 earnings that beat estimates, with revenue growth driven by its residential platform. The stock has shown volatility amid broader market trends but remains a key player in real estate tech.

ticker_hexa-b-st.name: Hexagon AB (publ)
ticker_hexa-b-st.blurb: Hexagon AB is a global technology company specializing in geospatial and industrial enterprise solutions. It operates through segments including Manufacturing Intelligence, Geosystems, Autonomous Solutions, and Octave, providing sensors, software, and autonomous solutions for various industries. The company is a leader in digital reality solutions, combining sensor, software, and autonomous technologies to improve efficiency and sustainability.
ticker_hexa-b-st.recent: On April 23, 2026, Hexagon reported first-quarter earnings that were broadly in line with expectations, with shares considered fairly valued according to Morningstar. The stock has traded in a 52-week range of 88.52 to 122.10 SEK, with a recent price around 99-100 SEK. The company declared a dividend of 1.52 SEK per share with an ex-dividend date of April 27, 2026.
